fun_definition.description: The FUN-DEFINITION, for a project that ran prototype rounds: what the stakeholder found fun, which you write down and do not judge. Null for a project that did not, and only then.

body.description: What makes this game fun, in the stakeholder's findings and in their words where their notes give them. Introduce each element by its F-n id.

elements.description: One element per essential source of fun. Add only what the stakeholder found fun in the Decision Records you were given: never an element from general knowledge, and never one only the plans hypothesised.

id.description: F-1, F-2 and so on, each used once.

element.description: The element in a few words, on one line.

evidence.description: At least one pin of the form DEC-<id>@<version>#p-<k>: the Decision Record of a prototype round and the prototype in it that the stakeholder marked fun. A prototype they marked not fun, or a record that is not a prototype round's, is refused.

how_to_check.description: How a person playing would tell that this element still works, on one line.

target_artifact.description: The document id alone, such as SPEC-M1 or TEST-PLAN-M1, with no @version or #section.

target_section.description: The slug of the heading whose text you would replace, such as risks. Name this or target_ac, not both.

target_ac.description: A criterion id, such as AC-3. On a Spec, proposed_text is that criterion's new text, which the stakeholder decides. On a Test Plan, proposed_text is that criterion's new commands, one exact shell command per line.

proposed_text.description: The whole replacement for that section, criterion text or list of commands.

proposed_verification.description: Only with target_ac on a Spec: the one shell command its Verified by line should name instead, when that command is what is wrong. proposed_text still holds the criterion's text, word for word if only the command is wrong. On a Test Plan the commands are proposed_text, so leave this out.
